requirement:
By default, authoring MUST suppress per-subject `true` judgment lines and show
each `false` judgment's subject and outcome on stderr, on both terminals and
redirected output. Existing progress counters and completion summaries MUST remain
available; FIXME notices and authoring errors MUST remain visible. Single-subject
authoring MUST retain its subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and
usage-record metadata.

`-v` and `--verbose` MUST additionally show each false judgment's recorded Markdown
rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded
input snapshots. Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result,
without additional inference. In `--stdout` mode, stdout MUST remain only the
evidence JSON; verbose rationale and other diagnostics MUST go to stderr.
Verbosity MUST NOT change persistence, validation, or exit-status rules.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.invocation` {cite}`requirements.authoring.batch`
rationale:
**Judgment: true.** The code marked {impl} covers each obligation in `requirements.authoring.reporting`, and the tests cover the main cases. The one thing I'd note is the `-v` flag declaration, covered below.

**Batch (`--all`) implementation**
- `BatchProgress::completed` (src/authoring/progress.rs:93-120) is marked {impl}.
  - It prints nothing for a `true` judgment, so per-subject true lines are suppressed.
  - For `false`, it prints `"<subject>: false (usage: …)"`. It appends the stored `assessment.rationale` only when `verbose` is set.
  - For FIXME, it prints a notice that is always visible.
- `BatchProgress::failed` prints authoring errors to the progress bar or to stderr.
- `BatchProgress::println` sends output through the bar on terminals and `eprintln!` otherwise, so output reaches stderr on terminals and on redirected output.
- The progress counters and the stdout completion summary (`"N authored; M unchanged; K failed"`) are unchanged. `author_all_with_options` creates `BatchProgress::new(options.verbose)` and reuses the existing assessment result, so reporting needs no extra inference.
- Verbosity is read only inside the rationale printing. It does not affect persistence, validation, or exit status.
- Rationales for true judgments are never printed, and input snapshots are never appended.

**Single-subject implementation** (the `Command::Author` arm of `main`, src/main.rs, marked {impl})
- A false judgment prints `"<subject>: false"` to stderr, with `outcome.rationale` added under `-v`.
- True judgments get no extra line.
- The `subject: backend / model` summary, the evidence destination and the usage path are all kept. In `--stdout` mode, stdout carries only the evidence JSON and the summary goes to stderr.
- A FIXME judgment adds `— FIXME` to the summary line.
- Exit status does not depend on `verbose`.

**Tests**
- tests/authoring_batch.rs
  - `batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose` runs batch mode with and without `--verbose`. It checks that true lines and true rationales are absent, the false rationale appears only under verbose, the FIXME notice and authoring error remain, no input source text leaks, there are no escape codes in redirected stderr, and the stdout summary is unchanged.
  - `terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors` and `verbose_false_rationale_is_readable_above_terminal_progress` run under a PTY. They check the progress counters, the false and FIXME lines, the absence of rationales by default, and rationale visibility with `-v`.
  - `failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure` covers error reporting and the nonzero exit status.
- tests/authoring_cli.rs
  - `false_is_a_completed_assessment` checks that the false line goes to stderr, not stdout, and that the rationale is hidden by default.
  - `verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs` runs single-subject mode with `-v` and `--verbose`, for false and true judgments. It checks that only a false rationale is shown, that it appears on stderr and not stdout, that no source text leaks, and that the evidence is persisted.
  - `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` covers `--stdout` with true, false and FIXME judgments, with and without verbose. It checks that stdout is pure JSON, that metadata and the false line go to stderr, that the rationale appears only for verbose false, and that the evidence and usage records are written.

**Residual note.** The `verbose` arg declaration in `enum Command` (src/main.rs) has no {impl} marker of its own. The behavior it feeds is marked in the `main` arm, so I don't count this as a gap.

:::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]` MUST assess one
existing requirement or named example in the current project. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} batch
`habeas author --all [--config <name>] [-v|--verbose]` MUST author every current requirement
and named example whose evidence is missing, stale, or invalid. It MUST preserve
current records without invoking a model for them, including accepted FIXME
judgments and current false judgments. A current false judgment is reassessed
only when its subject or inputs change, or when it is named explicitly with
{cite}`requirements.authoring.invocation`.
`--all` MUST be mutually exclusive with a subject name and `--stdout`.
Failure to discover declarations or parse project sources MUST report an error,
not a successful empty batch. A batch with no assessments needed MUST succeed
without resolving model configuration or credentials.
Each subject MUST receive an independent assessment with its own prompt, inputs,
judgment, and usage record. The command MUST report aggregate completion and each
authoring error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.reporting`, and retain
successful writes when another assessment fails. It MUST return a nonzero
exit status if any assessment fails. False judgments MUST still be written as
completed assessments; they remain failures under ordinary evidence validation.
An access-policy denial MUST abort only the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
The bundled Habeas skills MUST direct the supervising agent to run this command
to create or refresh evidence. They MUST leave judgments, rationales, and input
snapshots to the authoring harness; the supervising agent addresses findings by
changing requirements, source citations, implementation, or tests.
